title: The Nepal Himalaya winter earthquake excess did not continue in 2011-2026 at magnitude 4 and above in three catalogs, and GRACE water load did not predict monthly rates
abstract: Question: Bettinelli et al. (2008) reported that Nepal Himalaya earthquakes occur about two times more often in winter than in summer (NSC catalog, 1995-2000), and they linked this to seasonal water load. Does the cycle continue after 2010, does it occur in independent catalogs, and does measured water load predict it? Approach: we used the Nepal national catalog (NEMRC, ML 4 and above, 1994-2026), USGS ComCat (M 4 and above, 1973-2026) and the ISC Bulletin (mb 4 and ML 3 and above, 1990-2026) in a Nepal box (26.3-30.6N, 80.0-88.3E). We declustered with Gardner-Knopoff windows and removed the 2015 Gorkha zone for 3 years. The statistic is the winter-phase amplitude a_w (rate 1 + a_w cos(phase - 15 January); the 2:1 cycle is a_w = 0.37). We set the primary test (NEMRC, 2011-2026) before we computed any seasonal value. Inference used year bootstraps and a per-year random phase-shift null. We also fitted Poisson models of monthly counts on CSR GRACE water storage (2002-2026) with year fixed effects. Results: the primary a_w was -0.02 (95% CI -0.22 to +0.17, p = 0.56, n = 203). The sample had 99% power for a_w = 0.37 and 44% power for 0.15. ComCat and ISC also gave no winter excess in 2011-2026 (a_w -0.16 to +0.05). Before 2011, ComCat and ISC showed a weak winter excess (a_w mostly 0.11-0.23), but it changed with the declustering method. NEMRC gave +0.12 (-0.14 to +0.31) for 1995-2010. ISC events of ML 3 and above showed no cycle in any period (1990-2026 a_w +0.01, CI -0.07 to +0.09). The other Himalayan segments (NW, E) showed no winter excess. GRACE load anomaly and unloading rate did not change monthly rates (rate ratios 1.01-1.09 per SD, all CIs include 1; actual load added nothing to the mean cycle). Conclusion: at magnitude 4 and above, the data reject the published 2:1 winter cycle for 2011-2026, and water load does not predict monthly rates. A weak cycle of up to about 30% is not excluded at M 4. Limitations: we did not have the NSC catalog below ML 4, which the original study used, and the ISC ML sample combines agencies with changing detection; simple declustering; regional load index instead of fault stress.

display.caption: Winter-phase amplitude a_w of declustered seismicity with 95% year-bootstrap intervals, by catalog, magnitude cut-off and period. Blue: before 2011. Orange: 2011-2026 (squares: post-Gorkha 2018-2026 subset). Diamonds: NW and E Himalaya ComCat boxes. Dashed line: the published 2:1 winter/summer cycle (a_w = 0.37). Dotted line: a 30% winter excess.

Monthly distribution of declustered Nepal Himalaya earthquakes, relative to the mean month, for four catalogs and two periods. The curves show the 2:1 winter/summer model and a 30% winter excess model.

Left: CSR RL06.3 GRACE/GRACE-FO water storage over 25-30.5N, 79-89E. Middle: monthly declustered rate against the seasonal storage anomaly (quintiles, 95% intervals). Right: rate ratios per SD from Poisson models with year fixed effects for an annual cosine, the climatological and actual storage anomaly, and the climatological and actual unloading rate.
